mcqs.question: Which of the following sequences correctly orders the listed metals from the most reactive to the least reactive?

options.A: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
options.B: K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Fe > Zn > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
options.C: Na > K > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
options.D: K > Na > Mg > Ca > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt

mcqs.answer: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au > Pt
mcqs.explanation: The standard reactivity series (most to least reactive) is K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Sn, Pb, H, Cu, Ag, Au, Pt. Option A matches this order exactly; the other options have metals placed out of their correct positions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following displacement reactions will NOT occur under standard conditions?
mcqs.explanation: A displacement reaction proceeds only when the metal placed in the solution is higher in the reactivity series than the metal ion in solution. Zn, Fe and Mg are all above Cu, so reactions A, B and C are possible. Copper is lower than silver, so it cannot displace silver; therefore reaction D will not occur.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: When a metal that is higher in the reactivity series is placed in a solution of a salt of a metal lower in the series, what is observed?

options.B: The solid metal dissolves and the lower‑reactivity metal precipitates out of the solution.
options.C: Only a gas is evolved without any solid formation.
options.D: The colour of the solution changes but no solid forms.

mcqs.answer: The solid metal dissolves and the lower‑reactivity metal precipitates out of the solution.
mcqs.explanation: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace the ion of a less reactive metal from its salt solution. The more reactive metal goes into solution as its salt, while the less reactive metal is deposited as a solid.

mcqs.question:
Which metal is more reactive according to the reactivity series?
A) Magnesium
B) Iron
C) Both are equally reactive
D) Neither reacts with water
mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, magnesium (Mg) appears above iron (Fe), indicating that magnesium is more reactive. Therefore option A is correct; iron is less reactive, and both metals do react (magnesium more readily) with certain reagents.

mcqs.question: Select the list that correctly represents the general reactivity series from the most reactive to the least reactive metal.

options.A: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au
options.B: Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al, Fe, Zn, Cu, Ag, Au
options.C: K, Ca, Na, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au
options.D: K, Na, Mg, Ca, Al, Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au

mcqs.answer: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au
mcqs.explanation: The standard series (most to least reactive) begins with potassium (K) followed by sodium (Na), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), aluminium (Al), zinc (Zn), iron (Fe), copper (Cu), silver (Ag) and gold (Au). Option A follows this order; the other options have misplaced metals.

mcqs.question: Which metal can displace hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid?
mcqs.explanation: Metals that are above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from acids. Zinc is above hydrogen, so it reacts with dilute HCl to produce ZnCl₂ and H₂ gas. Copper, silver and gold are below hydrogen and do not react.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: When iron filings are added to a solution of copper(II) sulfate, which observation is correct?

options.A: Iron dissolves and a reddish‑brown deposit of copper metal forms.
options.C: Copper dissolves and a grey deposit of iron metal forms.
options.D: A white precipitate of iron sulfate forms without any metal deposition.

mcqs.answer: Iron dissolves and a reddish‑brown deposit of copper metal forms.
mcqs.explanation: Iron is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it displaces copper ions from CuSO₄. Iron goes into solution as FeSO₄, and elemental copper precipitates as a reddish‑brown solid. The other options describe impossible or incorrect outcomes.

mcqs.question: A student places separate strips of aluminium and zinc into two beakers, each containing copper(II) sulfate solution. Which observation best matches the reactivity series?

options.A: Copper metal deposits on both aluminium and zinc strips.
options.B: Copper deposits only on the aluminium strip.
options.C: Copper deposits only on the zinc strip.
options.D: No copper deposits on either strip.

mcqs.answer: Copper metal deposits on both aluminium and zinc strips.
mcqs.explanation: Both aluminium and zinc are above copper in the reactivity series, so each can displace copper ions from CuSO₄, leading to copper metal depositing on both strips. Options B, C and D contradict the series.
